title: Raising Ernie Jr. and Carmen; Carmen on the road
summary: Junior got a music scholarship but went to Howard; Carmen travelled with him and was hurt by segregated seating.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Talking about my children and grandchildren

blocks.x: We had a boy and a girl and a lot of my friends kid me and say undoubtedly I got Carmen by remote control. Carmen is, I think, about ten or twelve years younger than her brother, than Ernie Jr., and so anyway I started Ernie on the music very young and he did quite good; when he finished high school he got a scholarship, like football players and so on, athletes, but he got out of that real quick to go to Howard University, and I don't regret at all that it cost me.

after he began travelling, well I was proud that I had made the reputation that there wasn't anywhere that he went where he was ashamed to say that he was my son, and a lot of those promoters down south, all east and west, your dad played for me.
Then by me being in the booking business, he made a lot of nice contacts for me; so it worked out very nice.

My daughter started, she took piano and sang, but right quick she says I don't want to be a musician--she don't have anything against it, but I think as far as love, she loves me and Ernie does too, and she has nothing against any music, in fact, she used to travel with me. She would go along with me, but it's right funny, she was just tickled to death until one time we went to some club and they were so particular about it, they had to put her separate, she couldn't be where the ball was, and that hurt her. She said to her mother (inaudible).

I'll never forget, she was making the rounds once through Missouri, and that's when Jackie Robinson (inaudible), and I want to go to a baseball game and I had some night off, I think I played Springfield and was headed into St. Louis but I wanted to go the
night before to see the ballgame, and Carmen got tired and she was sleeping and she finally woke up and she said, daddy, this sure is a long road.
